@@ -0,0 +1,580 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+# ruff: noqa: SIM117
+import argparse
+import errno
+import os
+import socket
+from unittest import mock
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.launchers.utils.listen import (
+    _describe_port_holder,
+    cleanup_listen_socket,
+    setup_listen_address,
+)
+
+_MODULE = "vllm.entrypoints.launchers.utils.listen"
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Shared fixtures
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def make_args():
+    """Factory for a minimal ``argparse.Namespace`` resembling serve args."""
+
+    def _make(**overrides) -> argparse.Namespace:
+        defaults = {
+            "uds": None,
+            "host": None,
+            "port": 0,
+            "ssl_keyfile": None,
+            "ssl_certfile": None,
+        }
+        defaults.update(overrides)
+        return argparse.Namespace(**defaults)
+
+    return _make
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def ipv6_loopback_available() -> bool:
+    if not socket.has_ipv6:
+        return False
+    try:
+        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET6, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
+            s.bind(("::1", 0))
+        return True
+    except OSError:
+        return False
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def blocking_listener():
+    """Bind+listen on an ephemeral port and yield the (host, port)."""
+    blocker = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+    blocker.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
+    try:
+        blocker.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        blocker.listen()
+        yield blocker.getsockname()[:2]
+    finally:
+        blocker.close()
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: serving over a Unix domain socket
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestUnixSocketScenario:
+    """Everything related to ``--uds``: bind, stale-file detection, errors."""
+
+    def test_binds_and_returns_unix_address(self, make_args, tmp_path):
+        uds_path = str(tmp_path / "vllm.sock")
+        args = make_args(uds=uds_path)
+
+        listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+        try:
+            assert listen_address == f"unix:{uds_path}"
+            assert sock.family == socket.AF_UNIX
+            assert os.path.exists(uds_path)
+        finally:
+            cleanup_listen_socket(sock, uds_path)
+
+        assert not os.path.exists(uds_path)
+
+    def test_stale_socket_file_gives_actionable_error(self, make_args, tmp_path):
+        """A crashed prior run leaves a path-bound file; error must say so.
+
+        Port-oriented hints ("free the port") would be confusing for UDS,
+        so verify none of them leak through.
+        """
+        uds_path = tmp_path / "stale.sock"
+        uds_path.write_bytes(b"")  # bound to any regular file → EADDRINUSE
+        args = make_args(uds=str(uds_path))
+
+        with pytest.raises(OSError, match="already exists") as exc_info:
+            setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        msg = str(exc_info.value)
+        assert str(uds_path) in msg
+        assert "stale socket file" in msg
+        # Must NOT reuse TCP-oriented wording.
+        assert "--port" not in msg
+        assert "SO_REUSEPORT" not in msg
+        assert "--api-server-count" not in msg
+
+    def test_other_oserror_propagates(self, make_args):
+        # Non-EADDRINUSE errors on the UDS path must be re-raised unchanged.
+        args = make_args(uds="/some/path")
+        err = OSError(errno.EACCES, "Permission denied")
+
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_unix_socket", side_effect=err):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError) as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        assert exc_info.value is err
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: serving over TCP (address construction only)
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestTcpBindScenario:
+    """TCP bind + ``listen_address`` construction, no conflict involved."""
+
+    def test_ephemeral_port_reports_real_port(self, make_args):
+        # ``--port 0`` must report the kernel-assigned port, not ``:0``.
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=0)
+
+        listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+        try:
+            bound_port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+            assert bound_port != 0
+            assert listen_address == f"http://127.0.0.1:{bound_port}"
+        finally:
+            sock.close()
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("host", [None, ""])
+    def test_default_host_is_0000(self, make_args, host):
+        # `None` and "" host must be displayed as 0.0.0.0, not `:port`.
+        args = make_args(host=host, port=0)
+
+        listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+        try:
+            bound_port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+            assert listen_address == f"http://0.0.0.0:{bound_port}"
+        finally:
+            sock.close()
+
+    def test_hostname_preserved(self, make_args):
+        # ``--host localhost`` must be preserved, not rewritten to
+        # ``127.0.0.1`` by getsockname().
+        args = make_args(host="localhost", port=0)
+
+        listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+        try:
+            bound_port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+            assert listen_address == f"http://localhost:{bound_port}"
+        finally:
+            sock.close()
+
+    def test_ipv6_address_is_bracketed(self, make_args, ipv6_loopback_available):
+        if not ipv6_loopback_available:
+            pytest.skip("IPv6 loopback not available")
+
+        args = make_args(host="::1", port=0)
+        listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+        try:
+            bound_port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+            assert listen_address == f"http://[::1]:{bound_port}"
+        finally:
+            sock.close()
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: serving over HTTPS
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestSslScenario:
+    """TLS affects the reported scheme (``https://`` vs ``http://``)."""
+
+    def test_both_key_and_cert_implies_https(self, make_args):
+        args = make_args(
+            host="127.0.0.1",
+            port=0,
+            ssl_keyfile="/tmp/key.pem",
+            ssl_certfile="/tmp/cert.pem",
+        )
+
+        listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+        try:
+            bound_port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+            assert listen_address == f"https://127.0.0.1:{bound_port}"
+        finally:
+            sock.close()
+
+    def test_partial_ssl_files_stays_http(self, make_args):
+        # Only one of keyfile/certfile: must NOT report https.
+        args = make_args(
+            host="127.0.0.1",
+            port=0,
+            ssl_keyfile="/tmp/key.pem",
+            ssl_certfile=None,
+        )
+
+        listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+        try:
+            assert listen_address.startswith("http://")
+        finally:
+            sock.close()
+
+    def test_missing_ssl_attrs_falls_back_to_http(self):
+        # ``args`` built by embedded callers may not carry these attributes.
+        args = argparse.Namespace(uds=None, host="127.0.0.1", port=0)
+        assert not hasattr(args, "ssl_keyfile")
+        assert not hasattr(args, "ssl_certfile")
+
+        listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+        try:
+            assert listen_address.startswith("http://")
+        finally:
+            sock.close()
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: --api-server-count > 1 (SO_REUSEPORT)
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestReusePortScenario:
+    """Sharing one TCP port across multiple API server processes."""
+
+    def test_two_sockets_share_same_port(self, make_args):
+        """With reuse_port=True, two sockets can bind the same port.
+
+        This is what enables ``api_server_count > 1`` in the launcher.
+        """
+        args1 = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=0)
+        _, sock1 = setup_listen_address(args1, reuse_port=True)
+        try:
+            port = sock1.getsockname()[1]
+            args2 = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=port)
+
+            _, sock2 = setup_listen_address(args2, reuse_port=True)
+            try:
+                assert sock2.getsockname()[1] == port
+            finally:
+                cleanup_listen_socket(sock2)
+        finally:
+            cleanup_listen_socket(sock1)
+
+    def test_reuse_port_forwarded_to_socket(self, make_args):
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=0)
+        fake_sock = mock.MagicMock(spec=socket.socket)
+        fake_sock.family = socket.AF_INET
+        fake_sock.getsockname.return_value = ("127.0.0.1", 12345)
+
+        with mock.patch(
+            f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", return_value=fake_sock
+        ) as create_mock:
+            listen_address, sock = setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=True)
+
+        create_mock.assert_called_once_with(("127.0.0.1", 0), reuse_port=True)
+        assert sock is fake_sock
+        assert listen_address == "http://127.0.0.1:12345"
+
+    def test_unsupported_platform_gives_actionable_error(self, make_args):
+        # Older kernels / unsupported platforms: SO_REUSEPORT setsockopt
+        # fails with ENOPROTOOPT. The hint must point at --api-server-count.
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
+        err = OSError(errno.ENOPROTOOPT, "Protocol not available")
+
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError, match="SO_REUSEPORT") as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=True)
+
+        msg = str(exc_info.value)
+        assert "not supported" in msg
+        assert "--api-server-count" in msg
+        assert exc_info.value.__cause__ is err
+
+    def test_unsupported_platform_without_reuse_port_propagates(self, make_args):
+        # ENOPROTOOPT without reuse_port is unrelated to SO_REUSEPORT; must
+        # propagate unchanged.
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
+        err = OSError(errno.ENOPROTOOPT, "Protocol not available")
+
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError) as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        assert exc_info.value is err
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: port already in use (EADDRINUSE)
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestPortConflictScenario:
+    """The user asked for a port that is already held by another process."""
+
+    def test_real_kernel_conflict(self, make_args, blocking_listener):
+        host, port = blocking_listener
+        args = make_args(host=host, port=port)
+
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port", return_value=None):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError, match="already in use") as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        msg = str(exc_info.value)
+        assert f"Port {port}" in msg
+        assert "unknown process" in msg
+
+    def test_message_preserves_original_error_and_queries_port(self, make_args):
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
+        err = OSError(errno.EADDRINUSE, "Address already in use")
+
+        with (
+            mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err),
+            mock.patch(
+                f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port", return_value=None
+            ) as find_mock,
+            pytest.raises(OSError, match="already in use") as exc_info,
+        ):
+            setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        assert exc_info.value.__cause__ is err
+        assert "Port 8000" in str(exc_info.value)
+        find_mock.assert_called_once_with(8000)
+
+    def test_holder_description_is_embedded(self, make_args):
+        # Previous tests mock the holder away; this one checks the actual
+        # holder description ends up in the raised message.
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
+        err = OSError(errno.EADDRINUSE, "Address already in use")
+
+        proc = mock.MagicMock()
+        proc.pid = 4321
+        proc.name.return_value = "nginx"
+        proc.cmdline.return_value = ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]
+
+        with (
+            mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err),
+            mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port", return_value=proc),
+        ):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError) as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        msg = str(exc_info.value)
+        assert "pid=4321" in msg
+        assert "name='nginx'" in msg
+        assert "cmd='nginx -g daemon off;'" in msg
+
+    def test_survives_holder_query_failure(self, make_args):
+        # macOS SIP denies psutil.net_connections(); the EADDRINUSE message
+        # must stay actionable even when the holder lookup itself fails.
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
+        err = OSError(errno.EADDRINUSE, "Address already in use")
+
+        with (
+            mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err),
+            mock.patch(
+                f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port",
+                side_effect=PermissionError("macOS SIP"),
+            ),
+            pytest.raises(OSError, match="already in use") as exc_info,
+        ):
+            setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        msg = str(exc_info.value)
+        assert "unknown process (query failed)" in msg
+        assert "Port 8000" in msg
+
+    def test_hint_suggests_reuse_port_when_not_enabled(self, make_args):
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
+        err = OSError(errno.EADDRINUSE, "Address already in use")
+
+        with (
+            mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err),
+            mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port", return_value=None),
+        ):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError) as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        msg = str(exc_info.value)
+        assert "SO_REUSEPORT" in msg
+        assert "--api-server-count > 1" in msg
+
+    def test_hint_does_not_suggest_reuse_port_when_already_enabled(self, make_args):
+        """When reuse_port=True, suggesting "enable SO_REUSEPORT" misleads.
+
+        The holder is the one missing the flag (or is a non-vLLM process),
+        so the user cannot act on that hint.
+        """
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
+        err = OSError(errno.EADDRINUSE, "Address already in use")
+
+        with (
+            mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err),
+            mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port", return_value=None),
+        ):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError) as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=True)
+
+        msg = str(exc_info.value)
+        assert "SO_REUSEPORT" in msg  # mention is fine
+        # Must NOT tell the user to enable SO_REUSEPORT — they already did.
+        assert "enable" not in msg.lower()
+        assert "--api-server-count" not in msg
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: insufficient privileges (EACCES)
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestPermissionScenario:
+    """Binding a privileged port (< 1024) as a non-root user."""
+
+    def test_error_message_points_at_privileges(self, make_args):
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=80)
+        err = OSError(errno.EACCES, "Permission denied")
+
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError, match="Permission denied binding") as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        msg = str(exc_info.value)
+        assert "127.0.0.1:80" in msg
+        assert "elevated privileges" in msg
+        assert exc_info.value.__cause__ is err
+
+    @pytest.mark.skipif(
+        os.geteuid() == 0,
+        reason="requires non-root (root can bind ports <1024)",
+    )
+    def test_real_kernel_denial(self, make_args):
+        # On a non-root Linux/macOS CI this exercises the real EACCES path.
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=80)
+        with pytest.raises(OSError, match="Permission denied binding"):
+            setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: unexpected OS error (must not be masked)
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestUnexpectedErrorScenario:
+    def test_unknown_oserror_propagates_unchanged(self, make_args):
+        args = make_args(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
+        err = OSError(errno.ENOMEM, "Out of memory")
+
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.create_server_socket", side_effect=err):
+            with pytest.raises(OSError) as exc_info:
+                setup_listen_address(args, reuse_port=False)
+
+        assert exc_info.value is err
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: socket cleanup (independent of how the socket was bound)
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestSocketCleanup:
+    """``cleanup_listen_socket`` must be safe and thorough in every case."""
+
+    def test_closes_tcp_socket(self):
+        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        assert sock.fileno() != -1
+
+        cleanup_listen_socket(sock)
+
+        assert sock.fileno() == -1
+
+    def test_swallows_close_error(self):
+        sock = mock.MagicMock(spec=socket.socket)
+        sock.family = socket.AF_INET
+        sock.close.side_effect = OSError("boom")
+
+        cleanup_listen_socket(sock)  # must not raise
+
+        sock.close.assert_called_once()
+
+    def test_unlinks_uds_with_explicit_path(self, tmp_path):
+        uds_path = str(tmp_path / "explicit.sock")
+        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+        sock.bind(uds_path)
+        assert os.path.exists(uds_path)
+
+        cleanup_listen_socket(sock, uds_path)
+
+        assert not os.path.exists(uds_path)
+        assert sock.fileno() == -1
+
+    def test_infers_uds_path_from_sock(self, tmp_path):
+        uds_path = str(tmp_path / "infer.sock")
+        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+        sock.bind(uds_path)
+        assert os.path.exists(uds_path)
+
+        cleanup_listen_socket(sock)  # no uds_path passed
+
+        assert not os.path.exists(uds_path)
+        assert sock.fileno() == -1
+
+    def test_idempotent(self, tmp_path):
+        uds_path = str(tmp_path / "idem.sock")
+        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+        sock.bind(uds_path)
+
+        cleanup_listen_socket(sock, uds_path)
+        cleanup_listen_socket(sock, uds_path)  # must not raise
+
+    def test_swallows_missing_uds_unlink(self, tmp_path):
+        uds_path = str(tmp_path / "never-created.sock")
+        sock = mock.MagicMock(spec=socket.socket)
+        sock.family = socket.AF_UNIX
+
+        cleanup_listen_socket(sock, uds_path)  # must not raise
+
+        sock.close.assert_called_once()
+
+
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Scenario: describing who holds the conflicting port
+# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+class TestPortHolderDescription:
+    """``_describe_port_holder`` is best-effort; must never raise."""
+
+    def test_no_process_found(self):
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port", return_value=None):
+            assert _describe_port_holder(8000) == "unknown process"
+
+    def test_query_failure(self):
+        # E.g. macOS SIP denies psutil.net_connections().
+        with mock.patch(
+            f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port",
+            side_effect=RuntimeError("psutil gone"),
+        ):
+            assert _describe_port_holder(8000) == "unknown process (query failed)"
+
+    def test_full_description(self):
+        proc = mock.MagicMock()
+        proc.pid = 1234
+        proc.name.return_value = "uvicorn"
+        proc.cmdline.return_value = ["uvicorn", "app:main"]
+
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port", return_value=proc):
+            result = _describe_port_holder(8000)
+
+        assert "pid=1234" in result
+        assert "name='uvicorn'" in result
+        assert "cmd='uvicorn app:main'" in result
+
+    def test_process_attr_access_fails(self):
+        # Permission-restricted process: pid is available, name/cmdline are not.
+        proc = mock.MagicMock()
+        proc.pid = 1234
+        proc.name.side_effect = RuntimeError("access denied")
+        proc.cmdline.side_effect = RuntimeError("access denied")
+
+        with mock.patch(f"{_MODULE}.find_process_using_port", return_value=proc):
+            result = _describe_port_holder(8000)
+
+        assert "pid=1234" in result
+        assert "name='<unavailable>'" in result
+        assert "cmd='<unavailable>'" in result

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import argparse
+import contextlib
+
+import vllm
+from vllm import envs
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.usage.usage_lib import UsageContext
+from vllm.v1.engine.utils import bind_engine_zmq_listeners, launch_core_engines
+from vllm.v1.executor import Executor
+from vllm.v1.utils import RustFrontendProcessManager, wait_for_completion_or_failure
+
+from ..cli_args import propagate_flash_late_interaction
+from ..launcher import create_server_socket, setup_server
+from ..utils import signal_utils
+from ..utils.listen import cleanup_listen_socket
+from ..utils.signal_utils import set_signal_handler, set_timeout, to_timeout
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def _run_rust_frontend(
+    rust_frontend_path: str,
+    args: argparse.Namespace,
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    num_api_servers: int,
+    exit_stack: contextlib.ExitStack,
+) -> None:
+    set_signal_handler()
+
+    listen_address, sock = setup_server(args, reuse_port=num_api_servers > 1)
+    exit_stack.callback(cleanup_listen_socket, sock, args.uds or None)
+
+    # `--grpc-port` is only accepted for the Rust frontend, which inherits this
+    # listener like the HTTP one. gRPC follows the HTTP TCP host, or IPv4
+    # loopback when HTTP uses a Unix socket.
+    grpc_sock = None
+    if args.grpc_port is not None:
+        grpc_host = "127.0.0.1" if args.uds else (args.host or "")
+        grpc_sock = create_server_socket((grpc_host, args.grpc_port), reuse_port=False)
+        exit_stack.callback(cleanup_listen_socket, grpc_sock)
+
+    executor_class = Executor.get_class(vllm_config)
+    log_stats = not args.disable_log_stats
+
+    parallel_config = vllm_config.parallel_config
+    dp_rank = parallel_config.data_parallel_rank
+    assert parallel_config.local_engines_only or dp_rank == 0
+
+    zmq_listeners = bind_engine_zmq_listeners(vllm_config, num_api_servers)
+
+    # Nested ExitStack so we can control exactly when
+    # `launch_core_engines.__exit__` runs: it must fire before
+    # `wait_for_completion_or_failure` because the CM performs engine-startup
+    # checks against `watched_frontend_processes` on exit. Attaching it
+    # directly to the outer stack would defer that check until after wait,
+    # changing error-detection timing.
+    engine_stack = exit_stack.enter_context(contextlib.ExitStack())
+    engine_launch = engine_stack.enter_context(
+        launch_core_engines(
+            vllm_config,
+            executor_class,
+            log_stats,
+            zmq_listeners.addresses,
+        )
+    )
+
+    local_engine_manager = engine_launch.engine_manager
+    coordinator = engine_launch.coordinator
+    stats_update_address = (
+        coordinator.get_stats_publish_address() if coordinator else None
+    )
+
+    if parallel_config.local_engines_only:
+        expected_engine_start_index = parallel_config.data_parallel_rank
+        expected_engine_count = parallel_config.data_parallel_size_local
+    else:
+        expected_engine_start_index = 0
+        expected_engine_count = parallel_config.data_parallel_size
+
+    api_server_manager = RustFrontendProcessManager(
+        binary_path=rust_frontend_path,
+        sock=sock,
+        grpc_sock=grpc_sock,
+        args=args,
+        input_listener=zmq_listeners.inputs[0],
+        output_listener=zmq_listeners.outputs[0],
+        engine_start_index=expected_engine_start_index,
+        engine_count=expected_engine_count,
+        data_parallel_size=parallel_config.data_parallel_size,
+        stats_update_address=stats_update_address,
+    )
+    engine_launch.watched_frontend_processes = api_server_manager.processes
+
+    # Equivalent to leaving `with launch_core_engines(...)` in the original
+    # code. `engine_stack` is still attached to the outer ExitStack, so if
+    # anything above raised, it would have been cleaned up there; close() is
+    # idempotent.
+    engine_stack.close()
+
+    def _coord_shutdown() -> None:
+        if coordinator is not None:
+            coordinator.shutdown(timeout=to_timeout(signal_utils.shutdown_by))
+
+    def _engine_shutdown() -> None:
+        if local_engine_manager is not None:
+            local_engine_manager.shutdown(timeout=to_timeout(signal_utils.shutdown_by))
+
+    def _api_shutdown() -> None:
+        # Matches `run_multi_api_server`: API servers get the full
+        # `shutdown_timeout`, while engine / coordinator get the remaining
+        # deadline. In practice the delta is a few microseconds.
+        timeout = (
+            vllm_config.shutdown_timeout if signal_utils.shutdown_requested else None
+        )
+        api_server_manager.shutdown(timeout=timeout)
+
+    # Register callbacks in reverse of the desired LIFO execution order:
+    #   set_timeout -> _api_shutdown -> _engine_shutdown -> _coord_shutdown
+    #   -> grpc_sock cleanup -> sock cleanup
+    if coordinator:
+        exit_stack.callback(_coord_shutdown)
+    if local_engine_manager:
+        exit_stack.callback(_engine_shutdown)
+    exit_stack.callback(_api_shutdown)
+
+    wait_for_completion_or_failure(
+        api_server_manager=api_server_manager,
+        engine_manager=local_engine_manager,
+        coordinator=coordinator,
+    )
+
+
+def run_rust_frontend(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
+    rust_frontend_path = (
+        envs.VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH if envs.VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND else None
+    )
+    num_api_servers: int = args.api_server_count
+
+    assert not args.headless
+    assert num_api_servers == 1, (
+        "VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH does not support api_server_count > 1"
+    )
+    assert rust_frontend_path is not None
+
+    # Reset residual signal state from any previous invocation (tests,
+    # embedded use). A stale `shutdown_by` deadline would make
+    # `to_timeout(shutdown_by)` return 0, forcing an immediate kill.
+    signal_utils.shutdown_requested = False
+    signal_utils.shutdown_by = None
+    signal_utils.timeout = None
+
+    engine_args = vllm.AsyncEngineArgs.from_cli_args(args)
+    propagate_flash_late_interaction(args, engine_args)
+    engine_args._api_process_count = num_api_servers
+    engine_args._api_process_rank = -1
+
+    usage_context = UsageContext.OPENAI_API_SERVER
+    vllm_config = engine_args.create_engine_config(usage_context=usage_context)
+
+    with contextlib.ExitStack() as exit_stack:
+        try:
+            _run_rust_frontend(
+                rust_frontend_path,
+                args,
+                vllm_config,
+                num_api_servers,
+                exit_stack,
+            )
+        except KeyboardInterrupt:
+            logger.info_once("[shutdown] API server: interrupted by user.")
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("[shutdown] API server: unexpected error during shutdown")
+            raise
+        finally:
+            # Register in `finally` so `set_timeout` also runs for the signal
+            # path (`SystemExit` raised by `set_signal_handler`, which bypasses
+            # both `except` clauses). Without it, graceful shutdown would fall
+            # back to the default 5s timeout instead of `shutdown_timeout`.
+            exit_stack.callback(set_timeout, vllm_config)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import argparse
+import contextlib
+import errno
+import os
+import socket
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.launchers.launcher import (
+    create_server_socket,
+    create_server_unix_socket,
+)
+from vllm.utils.network_utils import find_process_using_port, is_valid_ipv6_address
+
+
+def setup_listen_address(
+    args: argparse.Namespace, *, reuse_port: bool
+) -> tuple[str, socket.socket]:
+    """Bind the serve listen socket and return ``(listen_address, sock)``."""
+    # Bind before the engine starts to avoid race conditions with ray.
+    # See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/8204
+    if args.uds:
+        try:
+            sock = create_server_unix_socket(args.uds)
+        except OSError as e:
+            # `create_server_unix_socket` does not unlink a pre-existing
+            # socket file, so a crashed prior run leaves a stale path that
+            # surfaces here as EADDRINUSE. Port-oriented hints ("free the
+            # port") would be confusing for UDS, so give path-specific ones.
+            if e.errno == errno.EADDRINUSE:
+                raise OSError(
+                    f"Unix socket {args.uds!r} already exists. Another "
+                    f"process may be listening on it, or a previous run left "
+                    f"a stale socket file. Remove the file (rm {args.uds}) "
+                    f"if no process is using it, or pass a different --uds "
+                    f"path."
+                ) from e
+            raise
+        return f"unix:{args.uds}", sock
+
+    host = args.host or ""
+
+    try:
+        sock = create_server_socket((host, args.port), reuse_port=reuse_port)
+    except OSError as e:
+        if e.errno == errno.EADDRINUSE:
+            holder = _describe_port_holder(args.port)
+            if reuse_port:
+                hint = (
+                    "The holder does not share the port via SO_REUSEPORT "
+                    "(possibly a non-vLLM process or a different user). "
+                    "Free the port or pass a different --port."
+                )
+            else:
+                hint = (
+                    "Free the port, pass a different --port, or share it "
+                    "via SO_REUSEPORT by running multiple API servers "
+                    "(--api-server-count > 1)."
+                )
+            raise OSError(
+                f"Port {args.port} is already in use (holder: {holder}). {hint}"
+            ) from e
+        if e.errno == errno.EACCES:
+            raise OSError(
+                f"Permission denied binding to "
+                f"{host or '0.0.0.0'}:{args.port}. "
+                f"Ports below 1024 typically require elevated privileges."
+            ) from e
+        if e.errno == errno.ENOPROTOOPT and reuse_port:
+            raise OSError(
+                "SO_REUSEPORT is not supported on this platform. "
+                "Cannot use --api-server-count > 1 here; use a single "
+                "API server."
+            ) from e
+        raise
+
+    # Only the port needs to come from the kernel (so ``--port 0`` reports the
+    # real port). Keep the user-supplied host in the address so ``--host
+    # localhost`` still prints ``localhost`` instead of ``127.0.0.1``.
+    bound_addr, bound_port = sock.getsockname()[:2]
+    display_addr = host or bound_addr or "0.0.0.0"
+    is_ssl = bool(
+        getattr(args, "ssl_keyfile", None) and getattr(args, "ssl_certfile", None)
+    )
+    host_part = (
+        f"[{display_addr}]" if is_valid_ipv6_address(display_addr) else display_addr
+    )
+    listen_address = f"http{'s' if is_ssl else ''}://{host_part}:{bound_port}"
+
+    return listen_address, sock
+
+
+def cleanup_listen_socket(sock: socket.socket, uds_path: str | None = None) -> None:
+    """Release the serve listen socket bound by ``setup_listen_address``.
+
+    For AF_UNIX sockets the path is inferred from the socket itself when
+    ``uds_path`` is not provided, so callers don't have to remember to pass
+    ``args.uds``. Idempotent: safe to call multiple times (e.g. the shutdown
+    path may already have closed the socket).
+    """
+    if uds_path is None and sock.family == socket.AF_UNIX:
+        try:
+            name = sock.getsockname()
+            if isinstance(name, str) and name:
+                uds_path = name
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+
+    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
+        sock.close()
+    if uds_path:
+        with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError, OSError):
+            os.unlink(uds_path)
+
+
+def _describe_port_holder(port: int) -> str:
+    """Best-effort description of the process currently bound to ``port``."""
+    try:
+        process = find_process_using_port(port)
+    except Exception:
+        return "unknown process (query failed)"
+    if process is None:
+        return "unknown process"
+
+    try:
+        name = process.name()
+        cmdline = " ".join(process.cmdline())
+    except Exception:
+        name = cmdline = "<unavailable>"
+
+    return f"pid={process.pid} name={name!r} cmd={cmdline!r}"

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import signal
+import time
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+timeout: float | None = None
+shutdown_by: float | None = None
+shutdown_requested = False
+
+
+def to_timeout(deadline: float | None) -> float | None:
+    return deadline if deadline is None else max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.0)
+
+
+def signal_handler(signum, frame):
+    global shutdown_requested
+    logger.debug("Received %d signal.", signum)
+    if not shutdown_requested:
+        shutdown_requested = True
+        raise SystemExit
+
+
+def set_signal_handler() -> None:
+    global shutdown_requested, shutdown_by, timeout
+    shutdown_requested = False
+    shutdown_by = None
+    timeout = None
+
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal_handler)
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal_handler)
+
+
+def set_timeout(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> None:
+    global timeout, shutdown_by
+    if shutdown_requested:
+        timeout = vllm_config.shutdown_timeout
+        shutdown_by = time.monotonic() + timeout
+        logger.info("Waiting up to %d seconds for processes to exit", timeout)
